newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan top five carmakers' exports jumped in June.
newsitem.headline: Japan top five carmakers' exports jumped in June.

text.p: Japan's five major carmakers accelerated vehicle exports in June, helped by the weak yen and new models, according to figures released on Friday.
But industry analysts said that the rise was temporary and that automakers would be careful not to create new trade problems with the United States.

"I am sure trade friction with the United States will not revive. I don't think the current growth rate will continue (on their exports). They (Japanese carmakers) will curb their exports later this year because they know that sharp gains in exports will reignite trade friction," Koji Endo, a senior vice president of Lehman Brothers Japan Inc, said.
Japan's top carmaker Toyota Motor Corp said its exports rose 22.2 percent in June from a year earlier to 140,128, bringing its 1997 first half exports to 703,458, up 12.4 percent.
But its exports to the United States fell 0.3 percent from a year earlier to 40,791 units in June.
Honda Motor Co Ltd, the third-biggest carmaker, said its car exports jumped a steep 51.1 percent to 47,039, bringing its January-June total to 261,175, up 50.3 percent.
Of the total, its exports to the United States jumped by 128.2 percent to 25,769 in June, due to strong demand for the Civic compact and the CR-V light sport-utility vehicle.
"Our exports are at the level as planned -- 240,000 in 1997 (up from 151,633 in 1996) but will be little changed from the 1995 year level," a Honda spokesman said.
On Thursday, Andrew Card, the head of an influential U.S. auto makers group American Automobile Manufacturers Association (AAMA), criticised Japan's slow progress in opening up its automobile market.
While on a visit to Tokyo, Card said there would be political friction if Japan's surplus with the United States kept rising.
Japan's Finance Ministry said on Thursday the merchandise trade surplus with the United States grew 26.8 percent in June from a year earlier to 373.14 billion yen ($3.24 billion).
Imports of cars to Japan during the month dropped 24.1 percent from a year ago, while Tokyo's car exports jumped by 39.4 percent.

Concerns of a possible revival of trade tension have been in the headlines recently, exacerbated by U.S. President Bill Clinton's comments at last month's summit of the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations that Japan would risk an economic war with the United States if its trade surplus started exploding again.
Nobuaki Yanachi, a senior analyst of Kankaku Research, said the automakers would be careful to avoid that from happening.
"Top maker Toyota is paying very close attention not to stir up the United States," he said.

Mazda Motor Corp, 33.4 percent owned by Ford Motor Co, Nissan Motor Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Motors Corp also reported gains in their June exports by 51.3 percent, 31.3 percent and 25.8 percent respectively.
